pharm: Long-acting esterified progestin (norethisterone/norethindrone enanthate) that suppresses ovulation, thickens cervical mucus, and alters the endometrium after deep intramuscular injection.
quick: 200 mg by deep intramuscular injection every 8 weeks (may extend to every 12 weeks per local protocols)
Generally avoided in first 6 weeks postpartum; progestin-only otherwise acceptable per WHO
Contraindicated in active severe liver disease
Blood pressure, menstrual pattern, weight, pregnancy exclusion before injection
summary: Norethisterone enanthate (NET-EN) is a long-acting injectable progestin-only contraceptive given by deep intramuscular injection, widely used outside the United States under EMA, WHO, and national family-planning programs. It prevents pregnancy chiefly by suppressing ovulation, thickening cervical mucus, and altering the endometrium. It is given every 8 weeks (sometimes extended). It is not an FDA-approved drug in the United States. Common effects are menstrual irregularities (including amenorrhea), weight change, and headache. It is contraindicated in pregnancy, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding, severe liver disease, and hormone-sensitive cancers.
indications: Long-acting injectable contraception in women (prevention of pregnancy)

dosage.d: 200 mg given within the first 5 days of the menstrual cycle
dosage.n: Effective contraception begins promptly when started early in cycle
Some protocols allow up to every 12 weeks; do not delay beyond local window

dosage.d: 200 mg; may start from about 5-6 weeks postpartum per local guidance

admin: Administer by deep intramuscular injection into the gluteal muscle; do not give subcutaneously or intravenously
Give the first dose within the first 5 days of the menstrual cycle for immediate protection
Maintain the injection interval (every 8 weeks); counsel on the reinjection window per local protocol
Rotate injection sites and do not massage the site afterward
moa: Norethisterone enanthate is an esterified depot progestin that, after deep intramuscular injection, is slowly hydrolyzed to release norethisterone (norethindrone). The progestin suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, inhibiting the mid-cycle luteinizing hormone surge and thereby preventing ovulation. It also thickens cervical mucus to impede sperm penetration and renders the endometrium unfavorable for implantation. These combined effects provide reliable contraception for the duration of the injection interval.

absolute: Known or suspected hormone-dependent malignancy (e.g., breast cancer)
Active severe hepatic disease, liver tumors, or markedly impaired liver function
Known hypersensitivity to norethisterone or excipients
relative: History of thromboembolism or cardiovascular disease
Risk factors for reduced bone density (with prolonged use)

preg: Contraindicated in known or suspected pregnancy. Exclude pregnancy before each injection. There is no indication for use during pregnancy.
lact: Progestin-only methods are generally compatible with breastfeeding, but many guidelines advise avoiding initiation in the first 6 weeks postpartum. Small amounts of progestin pass into milk; follow WHO/national guidance on postpartum timing.
renal: No specific dose adjustment has been established for renal impairment. Use with general caution and monitor blood pressure and fluid retention.
hepatic: Contraindicated in active severe liver disease, liver tumors, or markedly impaired liver function. Progestins are hepatically metabolized; avoid in significant hepatic dysfunction.

major: Hepatic enzyme-inducing drugs (rifampicin/rifabutin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, certain HIV protease inhibitors/efavirenz, St John's wort) - increased progestin metabolism may reduce contraceptive efficacy
moderate: Lamotrigine - hormonal contraceptives may lower lamotrigine levels
Other CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors affecting progestin clearance
minor: May alter requirements for antidiabetic or antihypertensive therapy
interactions.diagnostics: May affect thyroid, adrenal, and liver function test results and some coagulation/lipid parameters.

rare: Reduced bone mineral density with prolonged use

monitoring: Exclusion of pregnancy before each dose
Bone health considerations with long-term use
counsel: Return on time for your repeat injection (about every 8 weeks) to stay protected
Irregular bleeding or no periods is common and usually not harmful, but report heavy or prolonged bleeding
This injection does not protect against sexually transmitted infections - use condoms for that
Tell your doctor about other medicines, especially for epilepsy, TB, or HIV, as they can reduce effectiveness
Seek urgent care for leg swelling/pain, chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, or yellowing of the skin
pk: Ovulation suppression within days of the first correctly timed injection
Serum norethisterone peaks within days as the ester is hydrolyzed
Depot release sustains levels over weeks; norethisterone elimination half-life ~ several hours
Contraceptive effect approximately 8 weeks per injection
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light; the oily solution may need warming before injection
pearls: Not FDA-approved in the United States; used under EMA/WHO/national programs - dosing reflects those sources, not an FDA label
Given every 8 weeks (shorter interval than DMPA's 12 weeks); maintain the reinjection schedule
Menstrual disturbance, including amenorrhea, is the most common reason for discontinuation - counsel up front
Enzyme-inducing drugs can reduce efficacy; review concomitant antiepileptics, rifampicin, and certain antiretrovirals
Return to fertility may be delayed after stopping, though generally faster than with DMPA
missed: If you are late for your scheduled injection, contact your clinic promptly. If you are beyond the recommended reinjection window, pregnancy must be excluded and additional (barrier) contraception used until the injection is restarted per local guidance.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with a single depot injection; effects would relate to exaggerated progestin actions (nausea, irregular bleeding). There is no specific antidote; manage supportively.
